Example 5 shows that the Component Test does not apply when the domain of the field is not simply connected. However, if we change the domain in the example so that it is restricted to the ball of radius 1 centered at the point (2, 2, 2), or to any similar ball-shaped region which does not contain a piece of the z-axis, then this new domain D is simply con- nected. Now the partial derivative Equations (2), as well as all the assumptions of the Com- ponent Test, are satisfied. In this new situation, the field F in Example 5 is conservative on D.
